_note: Federal + multistate cut of the special-population matrix (US-OWN-005: all populations IN). State-specific treatments live in the annexes; each row names the annexes it routes to. Owner decision US-OWN-005 cannot be a source (tier owner, no URL).

resident_employee.treatment: Ordinary employee: FIT per W-4 and Pub. 15-T percentage/wage-bracket method; FICA employee+employer; FUTA and SUI employer-paid (SUI to the localization State); state income tax of the work State and, for residents working elsewhere, the residence State per its own rule (credit, difference withholding or reciprocity).

effects.income_tax: FIT Pub. 15-T 2026 Worksheet 1A; state withholding per annex
effects.social_security: OASDI 6.2%+6.2% to 184,500; Medicare 1.45%+1.45%; Additional Medicare 0.9% over 200,000; FUTA 0.6% net on 7,000; SUI per sui_state
effects.reporting: Form 941 quarterly, 940 annual, W-2 by 2027-02-01; state withholding and UI returns

non_resident_employee.treatment: Two meanings in the US build. (a) Nonresident alien of the US: graduated withholding with the Pub. 15-T NRA add-on (16,100/yr Table 2), W-4 per Notice 1392 (Single, NRA, no exempt), treaty-exempt wages via Form 8233 to Form 1042-S, commercial-traveler exception (<=90 days, <=3,000). (b) Nonresident of a State: work-State withholding subject to reciprocity certificates, day/dollar thresholds (AL/LA/WV 30 days, AZ 60, IL 30 working days), convenience rules (NY, PA, DE, NE; NJ/CT retaliatory) and federal transport/military-spouse limits.

effects.income_tax: NRA add-on for withholding only; 1042-S for treaty wages; state nonresident sourcing per m06 tables
effects.social_security: NRA add-on has no FICA/FUTA effect: FICA computed on actual wages as for residents; for state nonresidents SUI follows the localization test, not residence
effects.reporting: W-2 (or 1042-S for treaty-exempt wages, via IRIS); state nonresident withholding on the work-State return; W-2 boxes 15-20 up to two States

fixed_term_contract.treatment: No federal or general state statutory fixed-term regime: employment is at will (SD, TN rows as examples) and a contract for a fixed period is a matter of contract. Payroll treats a fixed-term worker exactly as any employee; expiry of the term is a separation and triggers the work State final-pay rule.

effects.income_tax: none: same withholding as any employee
effects.social_security: none: FICA/FUTA/SUI unchanged; UI benefit eligibility on separation is state law
effects.reporting: Separation: state final pay and any state separation notice (e.g. TN LB-0489 within 24h - annex); W-2 as usual

part_time.treatment: No federal part-time payroll regime: the FLSA minimum wage and 40-hour overtime apply per hour/workweek regardless of schedule; part-time hours count toward ACA full-time-equivalent employees (ALE test 50). State paid-sick-leave accrual is per hour worked (annexes).

effects.income_tax: none: same withholding method; wage-bracket/percentage method by pay period
effects.social_security: none: FICA from first dollar; SUI/PFML per State (some States have hours-based coverage)
effects.reporting: ACA: FTE count for ALE status (1094-C/1095-C); state UI reports with hours where required (e.g. WA hours + SOC)

officers_without_employment_contract.treatment: Corporate officers are employees for payroll: wages subject to FIT withholding, FICA and FUTA; state law includes corporate officers as employees for withholding (OK 68 O.S. 2385.1) and UI coverage (FL 443.1216(1)(a)). Directors fees and partner/sole-proprietor draws are not wages (self-employment, outside payroll). Statutory employees (four IRS categories) are FICA-only.

effects.income_tax: Officer wages: FIT withholding as any employee (state law includes officers, e.g. OK)
effects.social_security: FICA and FUTA on officer wages; SUI covers corporate officers (e.g. FL); some States allow officer exclusions (annexes)
effects.reporting: W-2 as any employee; statutory employees W-2 box 13

apprentices_and_trainees.treatment: No federal apprentice payroll regime: FLSA minimum wage applies (sub-minimum only under DOL certificates). Students: private-school/college students employed by their school are FICA and FUTA exempt; public school FICA exempt unless sec. 218; work-experience full-time students FICA taxable. States set learner rates (CA 85% for first 160 h; WA 14-15 year olds 85%).

effects.social_security: Student exemptions from FICA/FUTA as listed; state UI student exclusions (annexes)

maternity_paternity_parental.treatment: No federal paid parental leave for private employers: FMLA gives up to 12 workweeks job-protected leave in 12 months (may be unpaid; employer may require substitution of accrued paid leave). Paid leave comes from state PFML/TDI programmes (e.g. WA PFML 1.13%, MA PFML 0.88%, DC PFL 0.75% employer-only; CA SDI/PFL in the CA annex) - premiums withheld/paid by payroll, benefits paid by the State.

effects.income_tax: State PFML benefits paid by the State are not employer payroll; employee PFML contributions are W-2 wages (Rev. Rul. 2025-4)
effects.social_security: Employee/employer PFML contributions per State programme, capped as the State sets (e.g. MA cap = SS wage base)
effects.reporting: State PFML quarterly returns (e.g. MassTaxConnect); W-2 box 14 per State practice

work_accident_occupational_disease.treatment: Workers' compensation is state law and generally an insured employer cost outside payroll; payroll touches it where a State levies a per-employee fee or allows an employee deduction (NM Workers' Compensation fee on TRD-41431: employer 2.55 + employee fee per quarter; WA employee share of workers' comp premiums - WA annex). No federal payroll rule.

effects.income_tax: none at payroll: workers compensation benefits are not employer wages
effects.social_security: NM fee per covered employee per quarter (employer and employee parts); WA employee deduction; no federal levy
effects.reporting: NM TRD-41431 quarterly (fee + wage report); state annexes

sources.article: Pub. 15 sec. 15 (no federal WC rule listed)

termination_and_final_pay.treatment: Federal law does not require immediate final pay; final-pay timing and vacation payout are state law (annexes: e.g. SD next payday, NH 72 h, UT 24 h on discharge; ME/MT/WY payout of accrued vacation). Severance is wages for FIT, FICA and FUTA. WARN: 60 days notice for plant closing/mass layoff - pay in lieu is wages. W-2 for a terminated employee by Jan 31 (earlier on request).

effects.income_tax: Severance and pay in lieu are supplemental wages (22% optional / aggregate)
effects.social_security: Severance subject to FICA and FUTA
effects.reporting: W-2 by Jan 31; state separation notices where required

mid_month_joiner_and_leaver.treatment: No proration rule in federal law: withholding is computed on the wages paid in the pay period with the period frequency of Pub. 15-T (annualise x periods); a joiner files W-4 (and state certificate) at hire and is reported to the State Directory of New Hires within 20 days (shorter in many States); a leaver gets final pay under state law. Wage bases (OASDI, FUTA, SUI) run per employer per calendar year from the first payment.

effects.income_tax: Pub. 15-T per-period method on wages actually paid; no catch-up or proration
effects.social_security: Wage bases start at the first payment by this employer in the calendar year; successor employer carry-over for FUTA
effects.reporting: New-hire report within 20 days; W-2 for any part-year employee

annual_regularisation.treatment: There is no employer year-end income-tax regularisation: the employee settles at assessment (Form 1040 / state returns). The employer reconciles quarterly 941 to annual W-2/W-3, corrects with 941-X / W-2c, and stops OASDI at the wage base and starts Additional Medicare above 200,000 per employer. Excess OASDI from multiple employers is refunded at assessment, not by the employer.

effects.income_tax: none at payroll: assessment by the employee; W-4 exempt status renewed yearly
effects.social_security: Per-employer annual bases (OASDI 184,500; FUTA 7,000; SUI per State)
effects.reporting: W-2/W-3 by 2027-02-01 reconciled to four 941s; 940 annual; state annual reconciliations

overtime.treatment: FLSA: 1.5x the regular rate over 40 hours in a workweek, no federal daily overtime. States add daily overtime (CA 8h/12h and 7th day; AK over 8h; NV for under 18.00/h from 2026-07-01; CO, KY 7th day - annexes). P.L. 119-21 qualified-overtime deduction (premium half) operates at assessment; employer reports W-2 Box 12 TT; FICA unchanged.

effects.income_tax: Overtime is regular wages for withholding; deduction only via W-4 Step 4(b)
effects.reporting: W-2 Box 12 TT (qualified overtime) from TY2026

multiple_employers.treatment: Each employer withholds and applies wage bases independently: OASDI and FUTA bases are per employer (successor carry-over only on acquisition); Additional Medicare is triggered per employer at 200,000 regardless of total income. The employee coordinates FIT across jobs on W-4 Step 2 (multiple jobs) - Worksheet 1A line 1g is not subtracted when Step 2 is checked.

effects.income_tax: W-4 Step 2 checkbox changes the schedule (Step-2-checked thresholds) and line 1g
effects.social_security: Per-employer OASDI/FUTA/SUI bases; excess OASDI refunded at assessment; common-paymaster rules not researched

local_regimes.treatment: Local income/payroll taxes exist in a minority of States and are outside state reciprocity: PA EIT (higher of resident or work-municipality rate) and LST; Philadelphia wage tax 3.735%/3.425% from 2026-07-01; OH municipal and school-district taxes (base = Medicare wages less 125); MI city taxes (Detroit 2.4%/1.2%); IN county tax (changes January/October); MD county tax (to 3.30%); KY occupational taxes (Louisville 1.45% incl. TARC); NYC/Yonkers; OR transit levies. Per-locality detail in the annexes.

effects.income_tax: Local withholding by residence and/or work locality per local rule; W-2 boxes 18-20
effects.social_security: Local transit/payroll levies (OR state transit 0.1% employee; NY MCTMT employer) per US-OWN-007 scope
effects.reporting: Local returns per locality; W-2 boxes 18-20 up to two localities

local_regimes.ccg_location: m06_tax (local); annexes PA, OH, MI, IN, MD, KY, NY, OR

employer_type_and_size.treatment: Size and type thresholds change obligations: ACA ALE at 50 full-time incl. FTEs (1094-C/1095-C, e-file at 10+); deposit schedule by lookback liability (50,000 monthly/semiweekly; 100,000 next-day); household employers (FICA at 3,000, FUTA at 1,000/quarter, Schedule H); agricultural (150/2,500 tests, Form 943); government employers (no FUTA, sec. 218); state size tests (AR minimum wage 4+ employees; MA PFML employer share 25+; NE sick leave 11+; VA paid sick 50+ from 2027-07-01 - annexes).

effects.income_tax: Household FIT only by agreement; agricultural FIT/FICA from 150/2,500
effects.social_security: Household and agricultural thresholds; MA PFML <25 no employer share

mid_year_rate_change.treatment: Several 2026 values change mid-year and must be dated per payment date: DC minimum wage 18.40 from 2026-07-01; OR 15.55 from 2026-07-01; AK 14.00 from 2026-07-01; FL 15.00 from 2026-09-30; NV daily-OT rule from 2026-07-01; Philadelphia wage tax from 2026-07-01; OH withholding tables from 2026-08-01; GA 4.99% tables; IN county rates from 2026-10-01; ID tables 2026-07-23; Trump-account exclusion from 2026-07-04.

effects.income_tax: Withholding tables effective by payment date (OH 2026-08-01, IN county 2026-10-01, ID 2026-07-23)
effects.social_security: Rate changes on the effective date (none federal mid-year in 2026)
effects.reporting: Quarterly returns split by period; W-2 annual totals

special_pay_cycles.treatment: Pub. 15-T supports daily/weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly/quarterly/semiannual/annual periods (annualise then divide). Supplemental pay (bonus, commissions, severance): flat 22% optional or aggregate; 37% mandatory above 1,000,000 per year. State pay-frequency and payday-timing rules (CA Lab. Code 204 semimonthly windows) and state supplemental rates (CA 10.23% bonus / 6.6% other) are annex detail.

effects.income_tax: Supplemental methods per Pub. 15 sec. 7; state supplemental rates
effects.social_security: none: FICA on all wages including supplemental

accrual_vs_payment.treatment: Federal payroll taxes follow the PAYMENT date: FIT, FICA and FUTA apply to wages paid in the calendar year (OASDI base for remuneration paid in 2026; W-2 on calendar-year basis; FUTA 7,000 per employer in the calendar year). Exception to watch: MA PFML rates apply to wages EARNED on/after 1 January. A December-earned/January-paid wage takes the new year rates and bases federally.

effects.income_tax: Withholding at payment; table year = payment date
effects.social_security: Wage bases by payment date; MA PFML by earning date

unresolved.why: Common-paymaster relief for related employers (multiple_employers row) was not researched in the FED unit.
unresolved.what_would_close_it: IRC 3121(s) / Pub. 15-A common paymaster section read into a FED row.

unresolved.why: Only NM fee and WA employee deduction are known; other States allowing employee workers-comp deductions not swept.
unresolved.what_would_close_it: Annex workers confirm per State (WA L&I rates; NM TRD-41431).
